From iOS 27.2 onwards, developers in the EU will be able to opt in to using an alternative version of the "App Tracking Transparency" system prompt, as part of a recent agreement between Apple and the EU. Here are the details.

New prompt is mandatory in some European countries

A few weeks ago, Apple confirmed it would comply with the EU's "fairer" App Tracking Transparency (ATT) rules, following an investigation by Germany's Federal Cartel Office.

This agreement brings to a close an antitrust investigation spanning several years, which focused on whether Apple's ATT rules placed third-party apps at an unfair disadvantage compared with its own apps. Apple has consistently denied the allegations, stressing that it fundamentally applies equally strict privacy principles to its own apps. However, German regulators were not convinced.

As a result, Apple has agreed to make eight adjustments to its ATT framework for Europe; full details can be found here.

That said, Apple today confirmed that iOS 27 will allow developers to choose whether to "use an alternative App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU", adding that "apps distributed only in Germany, France, Italy, Poland and Romania must use the alternative prompt due to legal requirements".

On an updated developer support page titled "User Privacy and Data Use", Apple further explained what this alternative system prompt contains:

The company also added that developers in the EU will be able to re-prompt users one year after their previous ATT choice, regardless of whether the user originally accepted or declined tracking.

For more information on the upcoming changes to ATT in Europe, click here.
